fatal_errors: Identifies coherent interfaces as the transition material, whereas the reported transition occurs in the λ = 16 nm Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer containing semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
Replaces the sputtered-coating nanoindentation experiment with unsupported molecular-dynamics simulations at high temperature and specified bulk stresses.
Invents a 20–30% creep-rate reduction, an interface-coherency threshold greater than 0.5, and a 15% falsification threshold without evidence.
Does not reconstruct the stress-exponent evidence distinguishing diffusion/interface-slip creep from dislocation-mediated creep.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes that interface coherency can affect creep through dislocation and diffusion processes, so it has limited topical alignment. However, it misses the central result: the semicoherent λ = 16 nm FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer, not a generic coherent multilayer, showed the mechanism transition and strongest reported creep resistance. It also substitutes unrelated high-temperature simulation conditions for room-temperature 5 mN nanoindentation, uses the wrong baseline, and supplies unsupported quantitative predictions. Its proposed measurements could probe creep generally, but they lack the stress-exponent analysis and coherent/semicoherent/grain-boundary comparisons needed to test the reported transition.
